items.explanation: The claim overstates what Las Casas achieved. The New Laws of 1542 curbed the encomienda, but Spain then expanded African slavery under the asiento system. The accurate context is continuity in coerced labor with a change in who was coerced — from Native forced labor toward enslaved Africans.
items.fact_source: u1.md §The story — Las Casas helped win the New Laws of 1542 that curbed the encomienda; Spain began replacing Native forced labor with enslaved Africans under the asiento; §What the exam tests here — from encomienda to the New Laws to African slavery: coerced labor continues, but who is coerced changes

option_explanations.A: Wrong because the New Laws limited new grants of Native labor but did not abolish coerced labor.
option_explanations.B: Right because Las Casas curbed the encomienda while Spain simultaneously expanded enslaved African labor.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because the Valladolid debate produced no such freeing of workers.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because Las Casas campaigned against the encomienda; he did not defend it.

options: (A) The claim is accurate: the New Laws of 1542 permanently abolished the encomienda and all other coerced labor in Spanish America
(B) The claim is inaccurate: the New Laws curbed the encomienda, but Spain expanded enslaved African labor under the asiento
(C) The claim is accurate: the Valladolid debate convinced the Spanish crown to free all Native workers from forced labor
(D) The claim is inaccurate: Las Casas actually defended the encomienda system
items.stem: A student claims: 'Bartolome de las Casas's campaign ended forced labor in the Spanish colonies.' Which of the following best evaluates this claim in its historical context?

stimulus.text: Las Casas won the New Laws of 1542 limiting the encomienda. In the same era, Spain expanded the importation of enslaved Africans under the asiento monopoly contract.

items.explanation: St. Augustine was a military response to French intrusion: French Protestants had built Fort Caroline nearby, and Spain destroyed it and fortified St. Augustine to hold Florida against a rival empire. Imperial competition, not gold or trade, drove the settlement.
items.fact_source: u1.md §Key terms (St. Augustine, 1565) — Spanish settlement in Florida; §The story — Spanish conquest model vs. French trade model

option_explanations.A: Wrong because Florida held no gold deposits; the gold was in Mexico and Peru.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because the Spanish model rested on missions and control, not fur-trading partnerships.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because Potosi silver shipped through Caribbean ports and Havana, not Florida.
option_explanations.D: Right because Spain fortified Florida to block French Protestant colonization and secure its imperial claims.

options: (A) The discovery of gold deposits in Florida
(B) Spain's desire to establish a fur-trading partnership with Florida's Native peoples
(C) The need for a port to ship Potosi silver directly to Spain
(D) Competition with France, whose Protestant colonists had built Fort Caroline nearby
items.stem: Spain founded St. Augustine, Florida, in 1565 — the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental United States. Which broader development best explains why Spain established a fortified settlement there at that time?

stimulus.text: Spanish forces destroyed the French Fort Caroline in 1565 and immediately established the fortified town of St. Augustine on the Florida coast.

items.explanation: Portugal's voyages were commercial: finding a sea route to Asian spices that bypassed the overland routes. The caravel made long Atlantic sailing possible, and Columbus applied the same logic — reaching Asia by sea — when he sailed west with Spanish backing.
items.fact_source: u1.md §The story — Portugal had spent decades perfecting the caravel and creeping down the African coast in search of a sea route to Asian spices; Columbus sailed west hunting for Asia

option_explanations.A: Wrong because Europeans did not know the Mexica Empire existed when these voyages began.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because the voyages were commercial ventures for trade, not crusades.
option_explanations.C: Right because the search for direct access to Asian spices drove Portuguese navigation down the African coast.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because the North American fisheries competition developed later and involved different powers.

options: (A) Portugal's plan to conquer the Mexica Empire
(B) A crusade to recapture Jerusalem
(C) The search for a sea route to Asian spices bypassing overland trade
(D) Competition with England for control of North American fishing grounds
items.stem: In the 1400s, Portugal developed the caravel — a small, maneuverable ship with lateen sails — and sent expeditions progressively farther down the African coast. Which broader development best explains the context of these voyages?

stimulus.text: Portuguese caravels crept down the African coast across the 1400s, each voyage pushing farther in search of a sea route to the spice markets of Asia.

items.explanation: Casta paintings are evidence for how Spanish colonial society responded to widespread mixing: by creating a formal legal hierarchy that ranked people by ancestry. The paintings document the system's categories and the social order it enforced.
items.fact_source: u1.md §Key terms (Mestizaje and the casta system) — racial mixing in Spanish America and the elaborate legal hierarchy that ranked people by ancestry

option_explanations.A: Right because the paintings catalog the ancestry-based ranks of a society organized around them.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because mestizaje was extensive; the system was a response to mixing, not its prevention.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because enslaved Africans occupied the bottom of the hierarchy, not an equal rank.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because the casta system was a Spanish colonial creation, not a Native one.

options: (A) Spanish colonial society formally ranked social status by ancestry amid extensive racial mixing
(B) The Spanish crown successfully prevented all racial mixing between Europeans, Africans, and Native peoples in its colonies
(C) Enslaved Africans were legally classified as equals of Spanish settlers
(D) The casta system was created by Native leaders to preserve their own hierarchies
items.stem: In Spanish America, widespread mixing between Europeans, Africans, and Native peoples produced the casta system — an elaborate legal hierarchy ranking people by ancestry. A historian using casta paintings as evidence could most reasonably conclude that:

stimulus.text: Casta paintings from 1700s Mexico depict families of mixed ancestry, each labeled with its precise category in the colonial racial hierarchy.

items.explanation: The review stresses that the victories owed less to a handful of soldiers than to the real weapons: epidemic disease, which killed enormous numbers of Native people with no immunity, and alliances with Native peoples who had their own reasons to oppose Mexica and Inca rule.
items.fact_source: u1.md §The story — victories owed less to a handful of soldiers than to epidemic disease and alliances with Native peoples who had their own reasons to hate the Mexica and Inca

option_explanations.A: Wrong because Portuguese and other vessels also crossed the Atlantic; ships alone explain nothing.
option_explanations.B: Right because disease and Native alliances were the decisive factors alongside Spanish arms.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because both were large, organized tribute empires with substantial armies.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because Portugal supplied neither the soldiers nor the funding for these conquests.

options: (A) Only Spanish caravels possessed the naval technology needed to carry armies across the Atlantic in the early 1500s
(B) Epidemic disease devastated Native populations while Native alliances gave Spain crucial military support
(C) The Mexica and Inca had no organized armies, political structures, or tribute systems of their own
(D) Portugal provided the majority of the soldiers, funding, and supplies for both expeditions
items.stem: Small Spanish forces toppled the Mexica Empire (1519-1521) and seized the Inca ruler (1532) with astonishing speed. Which broader context is most important for explaining these rapid conquests?

stimulus.text: Cortes marched on Tenochtitlan with thousands of Tlaxcalan allies; Pizarro exploited divisions within the Inca Empire — and in both regions, epidemics were already killing far more people than any battle.

items.explanation: Winthrop spoke to Puritans fleeing religious persecution in England during the Reformation era. Massachusetts Bay (1630) was founded as a religious haven — a 'city upon a hill' meant to model a godly community under the eyes of a watching world.
items.fact_source: u2.md §The story — New England (Massachusetts Bay, 1630) was built by Puritan families seeking a 'city upon a hill'

option_explanations.A: Wrong because the Anglo-Spanish conflict did not drive Puritan migration to Massachusetts.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because the Puritans came to build their own community, not primarily to convert Native peoples.
option_explanations.C: Right because Puritan migration was driven by religious conflict in Reformation-era England.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because tobacco was a Chesapeake crop, not a New England one.

options: (A) England's war with Spain over Caribbean trade
(B) The English crown's plan to convert Native peoples to Protestant Christianity
(C) Puritan migration driven by England's religious conflicts
(D) The success of tobacco as a cash crop in Virginia
items.stem: 'We shall be as a city upon a hill, the eyes of all people are upon us.' — John Winthrop, 1630. Which broader development best explains the context of this statement?

stimulus.text: "We shall be as a city upon a hill, the eyes of all people are upon us." — John Winthrop, sermon to Puritan migrants aboard the Arbella, 1630.

items.explanation: The rebellion united poor Black and white Virginians against the governor. Historians argue this cross-racial alliance of the lower classes frightened the planter elite, who then favored enslaved African labor — workers who could never claim the liberties of Englishmen — over indentured servants.
items.fact_source: u2.md §The story — Bacon's Rebellion in 1676; many historians argue the planter elite drew a lesson from it, shifting decisively toward enslaved African labor that could never claim English liberties

option_explanations.A: Right because the planter lesson historians identify is fear of a united lower class, answered by a turn to racial slavery.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because planters did not grant land to freed servants; they moved toward enslaved labor instead.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because the 1705 codes came three decades after the rebellion; they were a consequence, not a cause.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because enslaved people joined the rebels; the rebellion showed solidarity across racial lines, which is what alarmed planters.

options: (A) The rebellion's cross-racial alliance of the poor frightened planters, who shifted toward enslaved African labor
(B) The rebellion convinced planters to abolish indentured servitude immediately and grant land to all freed servants
(C) The rebellion was caused by the Virginia slave codes of 1705
(D) The rebellion demonstrated that enslaved Africans would always side with the colonial government
items.stem: In 1676, poor Virginians — Black and white, servant and free — rose against Governor Berkeley in Bacon's Rebellion. Many historians argue the planter elite drew a lesson from it. Which statement best evaluates that historical argument?

stimulus.text: Bacon's Rebellion (1676): Virginia's servants, enslaved people, and poor farmers united against the colonial governor before the uprising was crushed.

items.explanation: The 1688 petition came from Quakers — religious dissenters whose faith produced moral opposition to slavery from the start. It shows abolitionist roots in religious dissent, even though the petition changed nothing for a century.
items.fact_source: u2.md §The story — the Germantown Quaker petition of 1688 shows moral opposition existed from the start, even if it changed nothing for a century

option_explanations.A: Wrong because the transatlantic slave trade was expanding, not declining, in the late 1600s.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because no such ruling existed; slavery remained legal in the colonies.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because the petition was a religious document, predating the Enlightenment's colonial influence.
option_explanations.D: Right because Quaker religious conviction produced the earliest organized moral opposition to slavery in English America.

options: (A) The economic decline of the transatlantic slave trade in the late 1600s, which made slavery unprofitable
(B) A ruling by an English court that slavery was illegal in the colonies
(C) The influence of Enlightenment philosophers on colonial assemblies
(D) Quaker moral opposition to slavery, the earliest organized antislavery tradition in English America
items.stem: 'These are the reasons why we are against the traffik of men-body.' — Germantown Quaker petition, 1688. Which broader development best explains the context of this document?

stimulus.text: "These are the reasons why we are against the traffik of men-body." — The Germantown Quaker petition against slavery, Pennsylvania, 1688.

items.explanation: South Carolina's rice plantations made the Lower South the most slave-dependent region; by the early 1700s enslaved people outnumbered free whites there. Stono erupted from that demographic reality, and the colony answered with an even harsher slave code.
items.fact_source: u2.md §The story — the Lower South became the most slave-dependent; by the early 1700s enslaved people outnumbered free whites in South Carolina; Stono Rebellion of 1739; South Carolina's harsher code after Stono

option_explanations.A: Wrong because the Great Awakening was a religious movement, not a cause of the slave uprising.
option_explanations.B: Right because the rice economy's enormous demand for enslaved labor created the demographic conditions for the largest mainland slave rebellion.
option_explanations.C: Wrong because Parliament did not abolish the slave trade until 1807, long after Stono.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because the planters' context was their own plantation system; the rebellion was directed against them.

options: (A) The arrival of the First Great Awakening in South Carolina
(B) South Carolina's rice-plantation economy, where enslaved people outnumbered free whites
(C) The British Parliament's abolition of the slave trade
(D) The military alliance between South Carolina planters and the Spanish colonial authorities in Florida
items.stem: The Stono Rebellion of 1739 was the largest uprising of enslaved people in the mainland colonies before the Revolution. Which broader development best explains the context in which it occurred?

stimulus.text: In September 1739, enslaved people in South Carolina rose in the largest mainland slave uprising before the Revolution; the colony responded with a harsher slave code.

items.explanation: Spain held New Mexico through the mission system, which demanded Native labor and suppressed Pueblo religion. The 1680 revolt belongs to the wider pattern of Indigenous resistance to European coercion — the same pattern seen in slave resistance and other Native uprisings.
items.fact_source: u2.md §The story — Spain held New Mexico (Santa Fe, 1610) through missions, until the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 drove the Spanish out for over a decade; §What the exam tests here — resistance from below: Stono, the Pueblo Revolt, and slave codes as cause-and-effect pairs

option_explanations.A: Wrong because France was not involved in the Pueblo Revolt.
option_explanations.B: Wrong because the Pueblos sought to expel the Spanish, not join the English.
option_explanations.C: Right because mission labor demands and religious suppression provoked a coordinated Indigenous revolt.
option_explanations.D: Wrong because no such territorial dispute existed between Spain and Portugal over New Mexico.

options: (A) French encouragement of Native attacks on Spanish missions
(B) The Pueblo's desire to join the English colonies
(C) Native resistance to Spanish mission labor demands and religious suppression
(D) A diplomatic dispute between Spain and Portugal over sovereignty in the New Mexico territory
items.stem: In 1680, Pueblo peoples under Pope coordinated an uprising that expelled Spanish colonists and missionaries from New Mexico for over a decade. Which broader development best explains the context of this revolt?

stimulus.text: The Pueblo Revolt of 1680: under the leader Pope, Pueblo communities drove every Spanish settler and missionary out of New Mexico for more than ten years.
